card.keepWhy: Unseen, and still it changes everything.
sources: John 3:1 (Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews)
John 3:2 (he came to Jesus by night: “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God”)
John 3:3 (“Unless one is born anew, he can’t see the Kingdom of God”; KJV “born again”)
John 3:4 (“How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb?”)
John 3:5-8 (born of water and Spirit; “You must be born anew”; “The wind blows where it wants to…”)
John 3:10 (Jesus calls him “the teacher of Israel”)
John 19:39 (Nicodemus, “who at first came to Jesus by night,” brings myrrh and aloes for the burial)
Greek pneuma = wind, breath, spirit (used in John 3:8); anōthen = again / from above
check: Pictures set the talk on a lamp-lit rooftop; John doesn’t say where. Art only, not in captions.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever wished you could start your whole life over? not a new job. a new you.
options: then you’re in good company. a very important man felt that way too.
then keep that day in mind. this one happens at night.
good. you’ve probably heard the phrase. here’s where it starts.

steps.line: Nicodemus was a respected teacher, a leader people looked up to. One night, he came to see Jesus.

steps.q: John’s gospel is full of light and dark. Right after this talk, Jesus speaks of people coming to the light. What might “at night” hint about Nicodemus?
o: He’s still in the dark, but moving toward the light
Night was the only time Jesus was free
steps.why: Many readers see a slow walk out of the dark: night here, then speaking up for Jesus later, then coming openly to bury him.

steps.line: “Teacher,” he said, “we know you’ve come from God.”
Jesus answered, “Unless someone is born again, he can’t see the kingdom of God.”
steps.label: John 3:3

steps.q: Jesus says you must be born again. How does Nicodemus take it?
o: He asks what he must do to earn it
He pictures it literally, and is baffled
steps.why: He pictures a grown man climbing back into the womb. Jesus is talking about a different kind of birth.

steps.line: Nicodemus was baffled. “How can a grown man be born again? Can he go back into his mother’s womb?”
Jesus said this birth is of the Spirit. “The wind blows where it wants. You hear it, but you don’t know where it comes from or where it’s going.”
steps.label: John 3:8

steps.q: You can’t see the wind, only what it moves. So how would you know someone has been born of the Spirit?
o: By the rules they now keep
By what changes in how they live
By how sure they sound about it
steps.why: Nobody sees wind, only the trees bending. Jesus says the Spirit is known the same way: by what it changes in a life.

steps.q: Jesus says the wind blows where it wants. In John’s Greek, why does that line land as a pun?
o: Wind and water sound almost the same
The word for wind also means birth
One word means both wind and Spirit
steps.why: Pneuma means wind, breath and spirit, so “born of the Spirit” and “the wind blows” use the same word. Hebrew’s ruach works the same way.

steps.line: Nicodemus appears again near the end of John’s gospel. When Jesus died, the man who first came at night came again, carrying spices to help bury him.
steps.label: John 19:39

steps.q: John says Nicodemus brought about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes for the burial. What does that amount suggest?
o: Just the usual for any funeral
A burial fit for a king
steps.why: About a hundred Roman pounds, far more than an ordinary burial. Many readers see a royal burial, and a man no longer hiding in the dark.

say: here’s what i love. nicodemus had status, learning and answers. and he still came at night with a question.
“born again” comes from this story. for christians it means a new life from God, a gift you receive, not something you earn.

steps.q: The Greek word Jesus used for “again” can also mean “from above.” What does that add to what he meant?
o: The new birth comes from God, not from trying harder
You have to be baptized a second time
Only people in heaven are born again
steps.why: Nicodemus pictured a second birth of the body. Jesus meant a birth from above, by the Spirit, something God gives.

today.say: tonight, like nicodemus, bring one honest question you carry about life or faith. write it down, ask someone you trust, or, if you like, pray it. your choice.
options: that’s exactly what he did. jesus didn’t send him away.
that’s okay. he came at night. there’s no rush.
